properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 24 at 12:46AM AKDT until October 24 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels most likely around 1.0 to 2.0 feet above
the normal highest tide line, with highest water levels
expected near Togiak.

* WHERE...Northern Bristol Bay Coast.

* WHEN...Now through 7AM Saturday

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low lying areas. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Bering front brings a prolonged period
of strong southerly winds towards the coast. These winds will
result in elevated water levels and high surf. This period of
winds will coincide with a high tidal cycle this evening and
push water levels 1.0 to 2.0 feet above the normal highest
tide line. Water levels are expected to quickly drop off
Saturday morning as winds decrease, alleviating coastal
concerns.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 4:40AM EDT until October 24 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level in
low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...In Delaware, Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches. In
New Jersey, Ocean and Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water remains trapped in the back bays
where we expect minor flooding to continue. Levels are slowly
lowering.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

including the Dry Tortugas, and Florida Bay.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 4:14AM EDT until October 27 at 12:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to
8 feet in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 2
of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until midnight EDT tonight.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon EDT Tuesday. For
the Beach Hazards Statement, through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Ocean overwash impacts will continue through at least
Tuesday, especially around high tide, in areas were dunes have
been compromised. NC-12 between the Basnight Bridge and Rodanthe
remains closed. The next high tide is around 630 AM today. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 1 PM today. Tide levels will continue to
rise with King Tide Cycle in place through the upcoming work-
week. The morning high tide will be the highest of the two daily
tides. King Tides peak Tuesday and Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

peak Tuesday and Wednesday.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 24 at 4:03AM AST until October 26 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE... Across the northern coastal areas including western
and eastern coastal areas.

* WHEN...Remains through Saturday afternoon

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 23 at 11:57PM AKDT until October 26 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 8 to
16 inches. Winds could gust as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...South Slopes of the Central Brooks Range.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Saturday to 10 PM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The snow will come in two waves. The first
will be on Saturday morning into Sunday morning with accumulations
around 4 to 8 inches. There will be a break with lighter snow
Sunday afternoon through Sunday night. Heavier snow returns Monday
morning and continues into the evening with an additional 4 to 8
inches of snow.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit 511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1
for the latest road conditions.

* WHERE...Upper Koyukuk Valley.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Saturday to 10 PM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The snow will come in two waves. Snow is more

expected. There will be a break with lighter snow Sunday afternoon
and night. On Monday, snow is likely in the morning with 2 to 4
inches expected but rain becomes more likely in the afternoon as
warmer temperatures intrude and this will limit snowfall totals.
Any rain will act as freezing rain and accrete on surfaces below
freezing. This could make for slick conditions early next week.
properties.instruction: Slow down and use caution while traveling.
